reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Price action on MSTR flipped against the short this week -- up from the ~$93 entry to $100.01 (+7.2%, including +3.26% on 8/7 alone), about halfway to the -15% stop -- while BTC itself sat flat near $64.9k, meaning the move is squeeze/beta-driven (dovish rate repricing after a weak jobs report lifted speculative proxies broadly) rather than a fundamental improvement in Strategy's business (Q2 posted an $8.22B net loss and the company is still selling BTC to raise cash). That's the identical pattern that has repeatedly stopped out GDX/GDXJ/SOXL shorts in this experiment. A momentum/price-action-regime discipline says respect that shift and cut size pre-emptively rather than risk being forced out at the stop, while the deteriorating fundamentals still support keeping a smaller fade position on. Trimming MSTR short 12%->7%, tightening stop -15%->-10% and TP +40%->+30% to reflect the now-live squeeze risk, and parking the freed capital in cash rather than chasing already-full-weight longs since nothing new broke out this week. Checked JPM and ELV directly (both fine, no reversal signal, analyst PTs still rising) and see no fresh news undermining UNP/V/PG/IJR/CVX -- held at weight.
novelty: Round 3 still shares zero overlapping tickers with the Round 2 GARP book (JPM/ELV/UNP/V/PG/IJR/CVX/MSTR vs. MSFT/GOOGL/AVGO/META/IWM/UNH/COST/XOM/TQQQ/COIN) -- 0% same-direction gross-weight overlap -- and runs on an entirely different discipline (price-action momentum/mean-reversion rotation vs. valuation-anchored GARP), so the <50% overlap constraint is satisfied by a wide margin.
